content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: likely disconnection of amide (C=O)N, then Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated acid (or its derivative), then sulfonamide formation.

Thus forward steps: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid and aniline (or amine). So retrosynthesis: break amide to give carboxylic acid (or acid chloride) and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). The amide is attached to the α,β-unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-... So the amide carbonyl is part of the chain attached to aromatic ring c2ccc(...). So we can disconnect at amide to give a carboxylic acid (or acid derivative) attached to the alkene (i.e., cinnamic acid derivative) and an aniline (c3ccccc3N). The aniline is a 2-aminobenzene? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an extra NH? Wait: Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an extra NH at para? Actually it's an aniline (aniline) with an extra NH at the same carbon? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an amino group attached to the aromatic ring (two amino groups? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon, and also the aromatic carbon has an N attached? Let's parse: N c3 c c c c c3 N. So there is an N attached to the aromatic carbon at position 1, and also an N attached to the aromatic carbon at position 6? Actually the SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N means an aniline with an amino group at one end and an amino group at the other? It is a diamine (p-phenylenediamine). So the amide attaches to one of the amine groups (the one attached to the carbonyl). So the amide is formed between the carboxylic acid and p-phenylenediamine (one amine used). So retrosynthesis: break amide to give p-phenylenediamine (or its protected form) and the α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) attached to the sulfonyl phenyl.

Next step: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So we can disconnect the double bond to give an aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The aldehyde is the aromatic ring bearing sulfonamide attached to it. So we need to have the sulfonamide attached to the aldehyde ring. So we need to have sulfonamide formation as another step: sulfonamide formed from sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the phenyl ring with sulfonyl group attached to the other phenyl). So we can disconnect the sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (SO2Cl attached to phenyl) and aniline (the phenyl ring with the aldehyde). So overall three steps: 1) amide formation, 2) Doebner modification, 3) sulfonamide formation.

Thus we need to propose specific precursors (SMILES) for each step.

Step 3 (retro): target -> sulfonamide precursor: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (Ar-CHO). The sulfonyl chloride is derived from the phenyl sulfonyl group attached to the first phenyl (the tolyl). The sulfonyl chloride SMILES: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1 (para-methyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). The aniline with aldehyde: O= Cc1ccc(N)cc1? Wait the aldehyde is attached to the phenyl that also has the sulfonamide attached. The original sulfonamide: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to the tolyl phenyl. So the aniline part is the phenyl ring (c2) bearing the aldehyde substituent (the /C=C/...). So the aniline is the phenyl ring with an NH (the sulfonamide nitrogen) attached to the sulfonyl group; after disconnection, we have the aniline (c2ccc(... )cc2) with an NH2 (instead of sulfonamide). So the SMILES for that aniline with aldehyde: O= Cc1ccc(N)cc1? But also the aldehyde is attached to the ring at the position where the double bond attaches. In the target, the substituent is /C=C/C(=O)N... attached to the phenyl ring at para position relative to the sulfonamide? Let's examine target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

So we have a tolyl ring (c1) with a sulfonamide attached to it: NS(=O)(=O)c2... The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (the first phenyl). The sulfonyl group attaches to second phenyl (c2) which has the α,β-unsaturated amide substituent at para position (maybe). So the second phenyl (c2) has the substituent /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N at one position (maybe para). So after breaking sulfonamide, we get sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1 (para-methyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). And the aniline is the second phenyl with an NH2 (instead of sulfonamide) and the α,β-unsaturated side chain? Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl, not the second. So after breaking, the second phenyl remains attached to the side chain but now has an NH2 at the position where the sulfonamide nitrogen was attached? Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl, not the second. The sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl. The sulfonamide is Ar1-NH-SO2-Ar2. So the nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (tolyl) and to the sulfonyl group. The sulfonyl group attaches to the second phenyl (c2). So after breaking, we get sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (Ar2-SO2Cl) and aniline (Ar1-NH2). So the aniline is the tolyl ring with NH2 (para-methyl aniline). So the aniline SMILES: Nc1ccc(C)cc1 (para-methyl aniline). The sulfonyl chloride is ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(cc1) (no methyl). Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl which has the side chain. The second phenyl also has the side chain (the α,β-unsaturated amide). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor must be the phenyl ring with the side chain (aldehyde) and sulfonyl chloride attached. So we need to have the side chain as aldehyde (since later Doebner will convert aldehyde to unsaturated acid). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor SMILES: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=O)cc1 (para-methyl? Actually the second phenyl does not have methyl; the methyl is on the first phenyl. The second phenyl has the side chain at para position relative to sulfonyl group. So the sulfonyl chloride is ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=O)cc1 (para-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). No methyl.

Thus step 3 retro: target -> (para-methyl aniline) + (para-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). Good.

Step 2 retro: The sulfonyl chloride precursor (with aldehyde) is derived from Doebner modification: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid). So we need to break the double bond to give aldehyde (the same as above) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So the precursor for step 2 is the aldehyde (para-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride) and malonic acid. After Doebner, we get the α,β-unsaturated acid (para-phenyl sulfonyl cinnamic acid). So the product of step 2 is the sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=CC(=O)Cl)cc1? Wait the product after Doebner is the unsaturated acid attached to the phenyl, but the sulfonyl group is still attached. The acid is a carboxylic acid (cinnamic acid). So the SMILES: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=CC(=O)O)cc1 (para-sulfonyl cinnamic acid). However the sulfonyl chloride is still ClS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl; but after Doebner we have the acid, not chloride. Actually the sulfonyl chloride is used later for sulfonamide formation, so we need the sulfonyl chloride after step 2? Wait order: In forward synthesis, we would first form sulfonyl chloride from sulfonic acid? Typically sulfonyl chloride is prepared from sulfonic acid (by thionyl chloride). But the guidance says sulfonamide formation occurs when an amine reacts with a sulfonyl chloride. So in retrosynthesis, we break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and amine. So the sulfonyl chloride must be present before sulfonamide formation. The unsaturated acid is attached to the phenyl that also has sulfonyl chloride. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor must have the unsaturated acid attached (cinnamic acid). So step 2 should produce the unsaturated acid attached to phenyl with sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is not formed in Doebner; it's a separate functional group. The Doebner modification forms the α,β-unsaturated acid from aldehyde and malonic acid. So the aldehyde precursor is the phenyl sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde substituent. After Doebner, we get phenyl sulfonyl chloride with α,β-unsaturated acid substituent (cinnamic acid). So step 2 retro: break the C=C double bond to give aldehyde (para-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride) + malonic acid. So the product of step 2 (forward) is the unsaturated acid with sulfonyl chloride. So the SMILES for that product: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=CC(=O)O)cc1 (para-sulfonyl cinnamic acid). Good.

Step 1 retro: break amide to give carboxylic acid (the unsaturated acid) and aniline (p-phenylenediamine). However the unsaturated acid is already present as part of the sulfonyl phenyl. The amide attaches to the unsaturated acid carbonyl. So after step 1, we have the unsaturated acid (the same as product of step 2) and the amine (p-phenylenediamine). The amine is Nc3ccccc3N (p-phenylenediamine). So step 1 retro: target -> unsaturated acid (ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=CC(=O)O)cc1) + p-phenylenediamine (Nc1ccccc1N). Wait the unsaturated acid also has the sulfonyl chloride? Actually after step 1 forward, we have amide formation between the unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) and p-phenylenediamine, giving the amide attached to the phenyl side chain. The sulfonyl chloride is still present as ClS(=O)(=O) attached to the phenyl. So the product after step 1 is the target molecule (which has sulfonamide already formed). Wait the order: In forward synthesis, we might first form the unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride, then convert the acid to amide with p-phenylenediamine (using coupling agent), then finally form sulfonamide with para-methyl aniline? Actually the sulfonamide is between the tolyl amine and the sulfonyl chloride attached to the phenyl. So the sulfonamide formation uses the tolyl amine (para-methyl aniline) and the sulfonyl chloride (which already has the unsaturated acid). So the order could be: 1) Doebner to make unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride; 2) amide coupling to attach p-phenylenediamine to the acid; 3) sulfonamide formation with para-methyl aniline. That matches three steps.

Thus retrosynthesis steps (reverse order): Step 1 (retro) break sulfonamide: target -> para-methyl aniline + sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated amide attached (i.e., the product after step 2 and 1). But we need to keep three steps: So we can define:

- Reaction 1 (retro): sulfonamide cleavage: target -> sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=CC(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc1) + para-methyl aniline (Cc1ccc(N)cc1). (Note the unsaturated amide still attached.)

- Reaction 2 (retro): amide cleavage: sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated amide -> sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid (ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=CC(=O)O)cc1) + p-phenylenediamine (Nc1ccccc1N). (Amide broken to acid + amine.)

- Reaction 3 (retro): C=C formation cleavage (Doebner): sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid -> sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde (ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=O)cc1) + malonic acid (C(C(=O)O)C(=O)O). (Break double bond.)

Thus we have three reactions.

Now we need to find template IDs for each transformation. We can search for templates matching these transformations.

First, sulfonamide formation (forward) corresponds to retro template where sulfonamide bond broken. We have earlier search results for sulfonamide formation: reaction_id 733 etc. The retro_smarts_template for sulfonamide formation is: [O;D1;H0:2]=[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])(-[c:4])-[NH;D2;+0:5]-[c:6]>>Cl-[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])(=[O;D1;H0:3])-[c:4].[NH2;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]

That is a retro where sulfonamide broken to sulfonyl chloride and amine. So template_id = 733 (reaction_id). We'll use template_id 733.

Second, amide formation (retro) breaking amide to acid + amine. Search for amide cleavage template. We saw reaction_id 1205701 with retro_smarts_template: [C:2]-[NH;D2;+0:1]-[c:3]>>O=C(-C-C-c1:c:c:c:c:c:1)-[N;H0;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[c:3] . That's a retro where amide broken to acid and amine. Template_id = 1205701.

Third, Doebner modification (retro) breaking C=C to aldehyde + malonic acid. Need template for α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. Search for template with functional groups broken: carboxylic acid? Actually Doebner forms unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid, breaking C-C bond and C-O bond. So retro would break C=C and C=O? Let's search for template where product is unsaturated acid and reactants are aldehyde + malonic acid. Use search with functional_groups_broken maybe "C-C double bonds" and "carboxylic acid"? But we need to find a template that matches our unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. Let's search for templates where product is unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) and reactants include aldehyde. Use search with molecule_smiles of unsaturated acid: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=CC(=O)O)cc1 and functional_groups_broken maybe "C-C double bonds".


Search for template with that product.
